title: ROS playoff/championship sims run on the OLDEST loaded season (2024), not the newest — sorted(snapshot.seasons, key=luck._season_sort_key) passes objects to a function typed for strings, so every season sorts equal
claimUnderTest: playoff_sim.py:467 `current_season = seasons_sorted[-1]` and the module docstring ('every unplayed regular-season matchup in the current season') claim the sim operates on the newest season. The prior audit attributed the degenerate odds to 'the last loaded season is complete (offseason)'.
observed: `_season_sort_key(season: str) -> int` does `int(season)` inside try/except (TypeError, ValueError). All four ROS call sites hand it a SeasonSnapshot OBJECT, not `s.season`, so int() raises TypeError and the key is 0 for EVERY season. sorted() is then a stable no-op and `[-1]` returns the LAST element of a newest-first list — the OLDEST season. On the live league (seasons 2026, 2025, 2024) the sims resolve current_season = 2024, status 'complete', 8 owners. The whole 2025 season is loaded and ignored. Every other module in the repo (luck.py:193, power.py:79, weekly_recap.py:613) passes `s.season` correctly; only src/ros/ does not.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.public_league.snapshot import build_public_snapshot;from src.api.league_registry import get_default_league;from src.public_league import luck;s=build_public_snapshot(get_default_league().sleeper_league_id, include_nfl_players=False);ss=sorted(s.seasons,key=luck._season_sort_key);print([x.season for x in ss],'-> current:',ss[-1].season, ss[-1].league['status'])"
reproduction.expected: 2026 (or 2025 as the newest season with results)
reproduction.actual: 2024, league status 'complete', 8 of the league's 12 current managers

numericProof.formula: expectedWins[o] == wins_2024[o] for all 8 owners (schedule is empty, so sim_wins never increments past the seeded record)

userImpact: Every number on /league -> Championship and /league -> Trade Deadline is a replay of a regular season that ended ~20 months ago. A manager reads '100.0% playoff odds' or '42.6% championship odds' as a forward-looking estimate for 2026 and buys or sells on it. The bug is not confined to the offseason: mid-2026 the sims would still be simulating 2024.

priorFinding.note: Confirms the degenerate output (playoffOdds in {0,1}, one-hot seedDistribution, integer expectedWins, worstPlayoffOddsSe 0.0) but REFUTES the stated root cause. It is not 'the last loaded season is complete'; the sim is not reading the last season at all. 2025 is loaded and skipped. One-line fix at 4 sites: key=lambda s: luck._season_sort_key(s.season).

whatWorks: Once a season is chosen, the seeding, tiebreak-by-PF and bracket code all execute; the arithmetic downstream of the wrong season is internally consistent.
rootCause: Type mismatch between `_season_sort_key(season: str)` and the SeasonSnapshot objects the four ROS call sites pass it, silently swallowed by `except (TypeError, ValueError): return 0`.
requiredRepair: Change `key=luck._season_sort_key` to `key=lambda s: luck._season_sort_key(s.season)` at src/ros/playoff_sim.py:464,546,562 and src/ros/power_v2.py:325. Then add an explicit preseason guard so a season with zero scored games returns honestly-unknown odds instead of falling back to a completed season.
dependencies: W17-F002 (the Seller mislabel) is downstream of this and of the missing-owner coercion.
